reviews.question: In a four-player standard game, how many Escape Pods are selected, how are they distributed and oriented, and which tokens start in the Intruder bag?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Four players use 3 randomly chosen Pods; place lowest number in A, next in B, alternate A/B; all Locked side up. 2. Bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults total).
reviews.expected_answer: Three random pods; lowest numbered in A, next B, next A, all Locked. Bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 7 Adults.
reviews.reason: Correctly gives three randomly selected Locked Pods in A/B/A and the complete seven-Adult starting bag.

reviews.question: How are Objectives filtered and dealt, when does each player choose one, what happens to the rejected card, and do Eggs trigger that choice?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Remove Corporate and Personal Objectives marked for player counts above the actual count; separately shuffle and deal one of each hidden. 2. Receive them before Character draft; choose one of the two at the First Encounter. 3. Remove rejected card face down, unseen by anyone. 4. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger the First Encounter choice.
reviews.expected_answer: Remove Objectives requiring more players than present; deal one Personal and one Corporate secretly. First Intruder miniature of any type appearing triggers immediate choice by everyone before resolving its Encounter. Remove rejected card face down unseen. Eggs do not trigger it.
reviews.reason: Filtering, separate hidden deal, choice at the named First Encounter, unseen removal and Egg exclusion are explicit. Calling the trigger First Encounter is an acceptable equivalent; the question does not demand a separate Encounter definition.

reviews.question: You use an Action card with printed cost 2 while holding that card, two other Action cards and two Contamination cards. What is discarded, and can Contamination substitute for payment? What if the card offers OR effects?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Discard the played Action card itself plus exactly two additional Action cards from hand. 2. Contamination cards can never pay Action costs, even though held; they remain in hand unless separately discarded by an allowed rule. 3. For OR sections choose one effect; still discard that card and pay its printed cost.
reviews.observed_evidence: Actions: Action Cost; Actions from Action cards
reviews.expected_answer: Discard the played card and two additional Action cards face up. Contamination cannot pay costs. Choose one OR effect.
reviews.reason: Explicitly discards the played card plus two additional Action cards, excludes Contamination payment and chooses one OR effect.

reviews.question: A Character in a burning Room takes one Action then passes. When do they take Fire damage, can they act again this Player Phase, can they discard cards, and do later players rounds burn them again?

requested_parts.reason: The normal-Action limitation is stated, but the surviving Interruption exception is not.

reviews.observed_answer: 1. Suffer 1 Light Wound only after finishing your own Player round in the burning Room, including a round ending by passing. 2. After passing, no more normal Actions this Player Phase. 3. On passing, may discard any number of hand cards. 4. Fire damage is assessed at the end of each of your rounds; later rounds you take no further turns once passed, so do not take repeated round damage that turn.
reviews.expected_answer: At end of own round take 1 Light Wound. Passing bars normal Actions this Player Phase, but official FAQ permits Interruption after passing. May discard any number of hand cards on passing. No further Fire wounds from later players rounds this turn.
reviews.reason: The end-of-own-round Light Wound, optional discard and absence of later Fire damage after passing are correct. The answer restricts normal Actions but omits the requested material exception that Interruption remains playable after passing.

reviews.question: Describe entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter, Exploration effect, Noise roll and token destination. How do Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination alter the Noise roll?

requested_parts.part: Reveal tile, set counter with exclusions, resolve and remove token
No Noise for an occupied destination
Silence/Danger Exploration cancels the movement Noise roll
requested_parts.reason: States If Room is empty, roll Noise and only discusses Danger/Silence as roll results; does not apply the Exploration cancellation.

reviews.observed_answer: 1. Flip the tile face up and resolve its Exploration token; set its Item count by rotating the tile so the token number faces the board's Item Counter (Nest/Slime excluded). 2. Remove the resolved token to the box. 3. If Room is empty, roll Noise; 1–4 places marker in connected numbered Corridor, including Technical Corridor if Entrance. If result is Danger/Silence, apply those effects instead; if anyone (Character or Intruder) already occupies destination, no Noise roll. 4. Silence means no effect, except Slime on Character converts to Danger. Danger moves all neighboring eligible Intruders not in Combat into Room; if none eligible, Noise in every connected Corridor lacking one. Door Exploration places Door in Corridor entered.
reviews.observed_evidence: Movement, Rooms, Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll
reviews.expected_answer: Reveal Room and Exploration token; set counter to token number except Nest/Slime Room; resolve effect and remove Exploration token from game. Roll Noise in empty Room unless Silence or Danger exploration cancels it. Occupied Room (Character or Intruder) gives no movement Noise roll.
reviews.reason: The tile, counter, token removal and occupied-Room exception are present. However the answer instructs a Noise roll whenever the destination is empty and describes Silence/Danger as results of that roll; it never exempts Silence/Danger Exploration tokens. Those Exploration results cancel the movement Noise roll, so the stated empty-Room instruction is materially wrong in the specifically asked cases.

reviews.question: What does Careful Movement cost and replace, when is it forbidden, and can a Closed Door be crossed or a miniature stop in a Corridor?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing Noise in a chosen connected Corridor of destination. 2. Forbidden in Combat and if all connected destination Corridors already have Noise; normal Movement restrictions apply. FAQ says it replaces automatic Silence/Danger results. 3. Closed Door blocks crossing. 4. Characters cannot stop in Corridors; only Rooms (Pods exception) can be occupied.
reviews.observed_evidence: Basic Actions; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors
reviews.expected_answer: Cost 2 Action cards; replaces post-movement Noise roll with placing Noise in a chosen connected Corridor. Forbidden in Combat or when all destination Corridors have Noise. Closed Doors block player movement; no miniature stops in Corridors.
reviews.reason: Gives cost two, chosen Noise placement, both prohibitions, Closed Door blocking and the no-stopping-in-Corridors rule.

reviews.question: You roll a number for a Corridor already holding Noise, with a Technical Corridors Entrance in your Room. Give the Encounter sequence, Noise removal, token destination and Surprise Attack comparison; do Contamination cards count?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. On trying to place Noise where a marker already lies, resolve Encounter: clear all Noise in Corridors connected to Room (Technical if Entrance), draw bag token and place matching miniature. 2. Set non-Blank token aside outside bag; if token causes Intruder to hide in Technical Corridors it returns to bag and loses Injury markers. 3. Compare token number with cards in triggering player's hand; fewer cards than token number causes Surprise Attack. 4. Action and Contamination cards both count for comparison; Contamination still cannot pay costs.
reviews.expected_answer: Resolve Encounter: remove all connected Noise including Technical Corridors; draw bag token; place matching Intruder; compare token number to all cards in triggering hand including Contamination. Fewer cards causes Surprise Attack against triggerer, equal or more does not. Set token aside.
reviews.reason: Gives connected Noise clearance including Technical Corridors, miniature placement, token set aside, and the fewer-hand-cards Surprise comparison counting Contamination.

reviews.question: How does Danger resolve with several eligible neighboring Intruders, and when none are eligible? Does moving an Intruder into your Room count as an Encounter? How does Slime affect Silence?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Danger moves ALL neighboring Intruders not in Combat with any Character into the Room. 2. If none (or all are in Combat), put Noise in every connected Corridor without a marker. 3. Intruder movement into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; they enter Combat. 4. Character Slime changes Silence to Danger.
reviews.expected_answer: Move all neighboring Intruders not in Combat into current Room. If none eligible, put Noise in each connected Corridor lacking it including Technical Corridors. Moving Intruder into occupied Room is Combat, not Encounter. Slime converts Silence Noise/exploration results to Danger.
reviews.reason: Explicitly moves all eligible neighboring Intruders, fills unmarked connected Corridors otherwise, distinguishes movement from Encounter and converts Silence with Slime.

reviews.question: During an Encounter you draw Blank. What happens to Noise and the Blank; when is an Adult added? Contrast Blank in bag development.
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Blank means no miniature appears; place Noise in every connected Corridor and return Blank to bag. 2. If it was the last token in bag, add an Adult token if one is available, otherwise none. 3. In bag development, Blank adds one Adult token if available and returns Blank to bag; no Encounter/noise specified.
reviews.expected_answer: Encounter replaces connected Noise in every Corridor; return Blank; add Adult only if Blank was last token in bag and a spare Adult is available; no miniature or Surprise Attack. Development always attempts adding one available Adult then returns Blank.
reviews.reason: Correctly restores connected Noise and Blank, limits Encounter Adult addition to last-token/available-spare conditions and contrasts unconditional available Adult addition during development.

reviews.question: Two Intruders attempt to move together from the same Room through one Closed Door. Where do they end, what happens to the Door, can it later close, and would a Noise-triggered appearance be blocked by that Door?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Both moving Intruders stay in origin Room. 2. They destroy the Closed Door simultaneously. 3. Destroyed Door lies down and cannot be closed again (except Plasma Torch). 4. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to appear through a Corridor with a Closed Door, the Door does not block the appearance.
reviews.expected_answer: Both stay in original Room and destroy Door simultaneously. Destroyed Door permits movement but cannot close except Plasma Torch. Noise-triggered appearance ignores Closed Door.
reviews.reason: Both moving Intruders remain and destroy the Door; the Plasma Torch exception and appearance ignoring Closed Doors are explicit.

reviews.question: An injured Intruder moves into Technical Corridors with Noise already there. What happens to its miniature, injuries, token and Noise? Can Characters or Doors normally use those Corridors?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Intruder disappears from board upon entering Technical Corridors. 2. Discard all its Injury markers. 3. Return its token to the bag; existing Noise on Technical Corridors stays. 4. Characters cannot use Corridors ordinarily (Mechanic Technical Corridors Action and Technical Corridor Plans exception); Doors cannot be placed there.
reviews.expected_answer: Remove miniature, discard injuries, return matching token to bag; keep Noise. Characters barred except Mechanic Technical Corridors card and Technical Corridor Plans Item; Doors never placed there.
reviews.reason: All four affected components are addressed: miniature removed, injuries discarded, token returned and Noise retained; Character exceptions and Door prohibition are given.

reviews.question: Describe an ordinary Shoot versus Melee Action: card/ammo costs, target location, Contamination, a miss, and the two-hit die result.
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Shoot costs 1 Action card and 1 Ammo, targets an Intruder in your Room with Weapon in Hand. 2. Melee costs 1 Action card and draws a Contamination card to top of discard before targeting Intruder in Room. 3. Melee miss gives Character 1 Serious Wound; Shoot miss has no wound penalty. 4. Double hit is 2 Injuries for Shoot before weapon modifiers, but only 1 Injury in Melee.
reviews.expected_answer: Both cost 1 Action card against target in same Room. Shoot needs Weapon in Hand and spends 1 Ammo; normal two-hit deals 2 injuries subject to Weapon. Melee draws Contamination to Action discard before choosing target, miss causes Serious Wound, two-hit deals only 1 injury.
reviews.reason: Same-Room targets, costs, Weapon/Ammo, ordinary Melee Contamination, miss effects and two-hit differences are explicit.

reviews.question: After damage, how are Larva, Adult and Queen death checked, when is a Carcass placed, and what if a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow?

requested_parts.required: Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; blood <= current total Injuries means death.
Draw 2 Intruder Attack cards, sum blood, and use the same <= current total Injuries death comparison. Accept a comparison established within this answer and a clear parallel Queen adaptation.
A dead Adult leaves a Carcass in its Room; a general non-Larva death rule suffices.
A dead Queen leaves a Carcass in its Room; a general non-Larva death rule suffices.
A dead Larva leaves no Carcass.
An arrow on either Queen card causes retreat in place of numerical death resolution. Accept an unconditional Queen-flees outcome following the normal numerical check. No reservation about precedence.

reviews.observed_answer: 1. Larva dies at 1 Injury. 2. Adult draws one Attack card and dies if blood value ≤ total Injuries; Queen draws two and sums blood, dies if sum ≤ injuries. 3. Dead Adult/Queen places Carcass in Room (Larva does not). 4. If either Queen check card has Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of death/endurance: move via Corridor on Event card; Queen retreats if either drawn card has arrow.
reviews.observed_evidence: Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat
reviews.expected_answer: Larva dies at 1 injury without Carcass. Adult draws one Attack card blood, dies if blood <= current injuries and leaves Carcass. Queen draws two, sums blood and compares same way; any Retreat arrow causes retreat via Event-card corridor number, discard Event, rather than normal numerical resolution.
reviews.reason: All seven adjudicated parts pass: Larva one-Injury death/no Carcass; Adult one-card <= check; Queen two-card sum <= check; Adult/Queen Carcasses; either Queen arrow replaces numerical death resolution. Event discard is outside this question's required parts.

reviews.question: A Character Escapes a Room with two Intruders toward an empty unexplored Room. When do attacks occur, who is targeted, what happens if they die, and what follows if they survive?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Escape is a 1-card Movement; before moving resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder present, largest first (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva). 2. Attack targets escaper. 3. If killed, Corpse stays in Room they tried to leave. 4. If survive, move to neighboring explored/unexplored Room; resolve normal exploration and Noise if destination empty.
reviews.expected_answer: Pay Movement cost 1, choose neighboring Room. Before moving resolve separate Attack from each Intruder targeting escaper. Death leaves Corpse in starting Room; survival completes move and standard exploration/Noise.
reviews.reason: Explicit separate pre-movement attacks target the escaper, death leaves the Corpse behind and survival completes ordinary exploration/Noise.

reviews.question: In an ordinary Intruder Attack with several Characters, how is the target chosen and ties broken; how is a hit determined; what changes for Larva and where does its Contamination go?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Intruder targets Character with fewest Action cards; tie goes to First Player token or next in turn order. Surprise Attack targets triggering Character. 2. Draw Attack card for non-Larva: matching type symbol hits/effect; otherwise miss. 3. Larva draws no Attack card. 4. Larva removed from board and placed on Character board; target gets Contamination card atop Action discard. If already has Larva, attacker disappears, existing Larva stays, Character only gains card and does not automatically die.
reviews.expected_answer: Fewest Action cards in hand; tie First Player or next in turn order. Matching attacker symbol on drawn Attack card means resolve effect; otherwise miss; ignore blood and discard card. Larva draws no Attack card: place miniature on target Character board and give Contamination on top of Action discard.
reviews.reason: Correct target selection/tie, matching-symbol hit test, Larva no-card exception, Larva placement and top-of-Action-discard Contamination are explicit. Attack-card discard and ignoring blood are not separately asked.

reviews.question: At three Serious Wounds, does dressing one prevent death from a Light Wound? What happens at a third Light Wound otherwise, what does Heal remove, and where do a dead Characters Corpse and Heavy Objects go?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Dressing only suppresses a Serious Wound's effect; it still counts, so at 3 Serious Wounds any additional Wound kills. 2. Third Light Wound clears Light track and causes Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or a Dressed Serious Wound as effect specifies. 4. On death place Corpse token in Room and drop Heavy Objects there; Item cards disappear from game.
reviews.observed_evidence: Character Wounds and death; Rules FAQ 24
reviews.expected_answer: No: dressed still counts; any further Wound kills at three Serious. Third Light clears Light track and causes Serious Wound. Heal removes specified Light Wound or discards dressed Serious card. Place Corpse and drop Heavy Objects in death Room.
reviews.reason: Dressed Serious Wounds still count at the fatal threshold; third-Light conversion, Heal and death locations match the key.

reviews.question: Contrast Canteen/Shower scanning with Surgery: which cards are scanned and removed, how is a Larva handled, and what costs or turn consequences follow Surgery?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Canteen/Shower scan all Contamination cards in hand only; remove non-Infected scanned cards. 2. Infected cards are kept; if no existing Larva place one; if Larva already present, Character dies and Creeper placed in Room. 3. Surgery scans all cards in deck, hand and discard; removes Infected cards and removes Larva if present. 4. Then suffer 1 Light Wound, automatically pass, shuffle entire hand and remaining cards into Action deck; hand empty until next turn.
reviews.expected_answer: Canteen/Shower optionally scan hand Contamination, remove non-Infected; infected gives Larva and retains card, existing Larva means death/Creeper. Canteen heals 1 Light; Shower removes Slime. Surgery scans deck/hand/discard, removes infected and Larva, then 1 Light Wound, automatic pass, shuffle all cards including hand into deck; empty hand until next turn.
reviews.reason: Correct hand-only ordinary scan/removal and infected outcomes contrast with all-zones Surgery, infected/Larva removal, Light Wound, automatic pass and full-hand reshuffle. Canteen healing and Shower Slime removal are outside the scanning comparison asked here.

reviews.question: How can uncarried Eggs be destroyed with Shoot/Melee, grenades, Molotov and Fire; which Melee penalties are waived, when is Noise rolled and when is the Nest destroyed?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Shoot or Melee attacks uncarried Eggs in your Room; each Injury destroys one Egg. Successful Egg Melee retains ordinary Contamination draw. 2. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; Molotov 1; Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg each Fire Damage step (2 with Vulnerability to Fire). 3. Missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor Wound; source leaves timing of normal pre-roll draw unresolved. 4. Noise roll after every single attempt to destroy Egg. Once no Eggs remain on Intruder board, Nest destroyed; mark with Injury.
reviews.observed_evidence: Eggs and the Nest; source limitations on missed Egg Melee
reviews.expected_answer: Each Injury from Shoot/Melee destroys 1 uncarried Egg. Successful Egg Melee retains the ordinary draw of 1 Contamination card onto the Action discard pile. On a missed Egg Melee, no Contamination card and no Wound are suffered. The sources do not specify how the normal pre-roll draw and miss waiver are reconciled; no refund or delayed draw is invented. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs, Molotov 1; Noise after every destruction attempt including miss. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg each Fire Damage step. Nest destroyed once all its Eggs taken/destroyed; mark Injury in Nest.
reviews.reason: All asked weapon counts, successful-Melee ordinary Contamination, missed-Melee waiver, Noise-after-every-attempt and empty-board Nest destruction are present. The unrequested missed-draw execution caveat is truthful context and does not reduce either grade under the coordinator clarification.

reviews.question: What permits or prevents entering an Escape Pod, what must you resolve first, how many Characters and Heavy Objects fit, and what are the options and consequences when you wait?

requested_parts.part: Entry cost, unlocked Pod, free space and no Section Intruder/Malfunction
Two Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space
Immediate launch or current-turn pass/wait with bag-development Noise
Later first-round wait/pass, launch or free exit and two Actions
Intruder appearance returns Pod occupants to Room
Malfunction blocks new entry but permits waiting/launch/exit
Second boarder can immediately launch both occupants
requested_parts.reason: No second-boarder launch authority is stated in this answer.

reviews.observed_answer: 1. Pay 2 cards for Section Room Action; Pod must be unlocked with free Character space; no Intruder or Malfunction in Section; roll Noise and fail if Intruder appears or is present. 2. Resolve Noise before entry. 3. Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. 4. On boarding may immediately launch; otherwise pass current turn and remain present for bag-development Noise. At start of each later Player Phase choose wait/pass, launch, or exit free to Section Room and take full 2-Action round. Intruder appearing sends Pod occupants to Room; Malfunction still permits wait/launch/exit but blocks new entry.
reviews.expected_answer: Use corresponding Evacuation Room Action cost 2, unlocked Pod with free space, no Intruder/Malfunction. Roll Noise first and fail if Intruder reaches Room. Two Character spaces; Heavy Objects use none. Enter then launch immediately or wait and pass current turn. At start of first round next Player Phase choose wait/pass, launch, or free exit followed by a full two-Action round. Intruder appearing in Section returns all Pod occupants; another boarder may immediately launch.
reviews.reason: Entry, pre-entry Noise, capacity, waiting pass/Noise, later choices, Intruder return and Malfunction consequences are given. The answer omits that another Character boarding the waiting Pod may immediately launch both occupants. Its phase-start wording is treated as shorthand for the later first-round choice, without inventing a different ruling.

reviews.question: Give the endgame checks in order. What happens with two Damaged Engines, a non-Earth destination (including Quarantine/Mars), and an infected survivor or one carrying a Larva? Do pod passengers need Contamination checks?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives. 2. Two or three Damaged Engines explode ship; everyone aboard dies, Pod passengers away. 3. Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters; Quarantine sleeper survives Mars. Ship is not destroyed and Intruders remain alive from non-Earth destination. 4. Every survivor, including Pod passenger: if no Larva, scan all Contamination cards from deck/hand/discard; only if any Infected (or Larva present) shuffle all Action and Contamination together and draw four; any Contamination in four kills. 5. Yes, Pod passengers undergo this check.
reviews.expected_answer: Engines then Coordinates then Contamination then Objectives. If ship survives to checks: two/three Damaged explodes kills all aboard incl Intruders; non-Earth kills sleepers but ship/Intruders survive, Quarantine sleeper survives Mars. All survivors including launched pod passengers scan all Contamination; any infected triggers shuffle all Action/Contamination draw 4, any Contamination kills else survives. Larva skips scanning and directly does shuffle/draw. Survivors then reveal/check chosen Objective.
reviews.reason: Correct check order, damaged-Engine destruction, non-Earth/Quarantine outcomes and final scan/shuffle/draw procedure, explicitly including Pod passengers and Larva bypassing the scan.

reviews.question: How are the basic and additional Room tiles and Exploration tokens placed at setup; what Coordinates, Destination, Time, Engines, Eggs and Weaknesses start on the board?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Random face-down Room 2 tiles fill 2 slots; Room 1 tiles fill 1 slots; random unseen Exploration token on each tile; extras returned unseen. 2. Random Coordinates face down Cockpit; Destination marker starts B; Time marker green. 3. Each of three Engines gets shuffled face-down Working and Damaged tokens stacked, top is true status. 4. Intruder board starts 5 Eggs and 3 random face-down Weaknesses.
reviews.expected_answer: All 11 basic tiles face down in 1 slots; five random additional tiles face down in 2 slots, leftovers boxed unseen; random face-down Exploration per tile. Random face-down Coordinates, Destination B, Time green. Each numbered Engine has shuffled Damaged/Working pair face down, top true status. Five Eggs, three random face-down Weaknesses.
reviews.reason: Fills the correctly numbered slots with unseen random face-down tiles/tokens and gives all requested board markers, Engine stacking, Eggs and Weaknesses. Slot-based placement is equivalent to enumerating tile counts here.

reviews.question: How are Player Numbers assigned and Characters drafted; what does each Character receive and where do Characters and the initial Corpse begin? Are Quest Items usable immediately?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Random Help card numbered to player count assigns number/order. 2. In number order each draws two Character draft cards publicly, keeps one, shuffles other back. 3. Each gets board, miniature in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10 Action cards, Starting Weapon in Hand loaded to capacity, and two Quest Items horizontal beside board; blue Corpse starts Hibernatorium. 4. Quest Items are not active until mini-quest condition flips them.
reviews.expected_answer: Random Help cards 1 through player count with matching Inventories assign Player Numbers; in number order draw two draft cards, reveal, choose one, shuffle other back. Receive board, ringed miniature in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10 Action cards, starting Weapon in Hand fully loaded, two horizontal inactive Quest Items; activate by printed quest then ordinary Items. Player 1 First Player; blue Corpse in Hibernatorium is Character Corpse Object.
reviews.reason: Numbered Help assignment, public two-card draft, Character starting equipment/locations, initial Corpse and inactive Quest Items are explicit. Extra setup context such as Player 1 receiving the First Player token is not demanded by this question.

reviews.question: When are Action hands refilled and the First Player token passed; what happens when the Action deck empties, and what are the normal discard destinations and visibility?

requested_parts.reason: No statement that markers return to their appropriate pools.

reviews.observed_answer: 1. Start Player Phase draw to 5, then pass First Player token left except first game turn. 2. If draw needed with empty Action deck, shuffle discard into new deck then draw. 3. Action discards face up to own discard; Contamination atop it, cannot pay; normal discards face up. Item cards go matching Item discard, Event/Attack/Wound to their respective discard; normal visibility face up. Search rejected Item goes face down bottom of chosen deck.
reviews.expected_answer: At Player Phase start draw to 5, shuffle Action discard whenever required draw finds empty deck; then pass token left except first turn. Actions/Contamination to own Action discard, Items/Event/Attack/Serious Wounds to respective discard piles face up; markers to pools. Search example has explicit face-down return exception.
reviews.reason: Hand refill/token timing, reshuffle and card discard visibility/destinations are present, including the Search exception. The question asks normal discard destinations generally, and the answer omits discarded markers returning to their appropriate pools.

reviews.question: Give the Event Phase order, which Intruders move on an Event card, what controls movement and when the event effect resolves; what happens when Event and Intruder Attack decks run out?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Advance Time (and Self-Destruct if active), Intruder Attacks, Fire damage/checks, Event movement, Event effect, bag development. 2. On Event move all Intruders of card symbol that are not in a Room with Characters. 3. They move to neighboring Room through Corridor number on card; Technical Corridor sends token to bag. Resolve card effect after movement. 4. Empty Event deck reshuffles discards; empty Intruder Attack deck reshuffles its discard.
reviews.expected_answer: Time and active Self-Destruct advance, Intruders in Combat attack, Fire Damage, Event card movement then effect, bag development fully resolved before next turn. Move symbol-matching Intruders without Characters in Room via card-number Corridor; ducts remove miniature/return token. Discard Event unless instructed otherwise. Empty Event/Attack decks reshuffle their respective discard piles.
reviews.reason: Correct Event Phase order, symbol/Character movement eligibility, numbered route, movement-before-effect and both deck reshuffles. Event-card discard is not independently asked.

reviews.question: In bag development, describe Larva, Creeper, Adult, Breeder and both Queen branches. Which tokens are removed or returned, who rolls Noise and when does the next turn begin?

requested_parts.part: Adult return before ordered non-Combat Noise
Breeder return after ordered non-Combat Noise
Queen placement branch is triggered by any Character in Nest
requested_parts.reason: Queen in Nest does not explicitly establish the Character-in-Nest condition; no such condition appears elsewhere in this answer.

requested_parts.part: Queen Encounter versus add-Egg outcome; Queen token returned
Resolve development and resulting effects before next turn

reviews.observed_answer: 1. Larva removed from bag, add Adult; Creeper removed, add Breeder; Adult returns immediately before all players roll Noise in order (skip Combat); Breeder prompts Noise rolls then returns. 2. Queen in Nest places miniature and Encounter; otherwise add Egg to board; Queen returns. 3. Blank adds Adult if available, then returns. 4. Adult/Breeder Noise rolls happen as specified; turn begins only after all development and resulting Encounters/Surprise Attacks resolve.
reviews.expected_answer: Larva removed to token pool, add Adult; Creeper removed to pool, add Breeder. Adult/Breeder cause ordered Noise rolls excluding Combat; token returns. For Adult specifically, return token immediately BEFORE Noise so same token may be redrawn in an Encounter. Queen: Characters in Nest means Queen there and Encounter; otherwise including undiscovered Nest add Egg; return Queen. Fully resolve triggered effects before new turn.
reviews.reason: Larva/Creeper upgrades, Adult-before-Noise and Breeder-after-Noise return, Combat exclusion and end-of-development timing are explicit. Queen text says Queen in Nest rather than stating that a Character being in the Nest triggers Queen placement; it never supplies that required branch condition. The Egg/return outcomes alone do not establish it.

reviews.question: When do Fire and Malfunction exhaustion end the game; what if the target Room already has that marker, and where do removed markers go? What happens to sleepers and Intruders when hull integrity is lost?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Attempting ninth Fire or Malfunction marker ends game: ship explodes/loses hull integrity. 2. Max one per Room; extra placements where Room already has marker do nothing. 3. Discarded markers return to appropriate pool. 4. Hull loss kills all aboard, awake or hibernating, plus Intruders and everything else aboard.
reviews.observed_evidence: Fire and Malfunction markers; End game
reviews.expected_answer: Eight of each; required new placement with no pool marker explodes/loses hull integrity, all aboard including sleepers/Intruders die. Existing same marker means nothing happens; max one per Room. Removed markers return to pools.
reviews.reason: Required ninth placement, existing-marker exception, pools and death of awake/sleeping Characters and Intruders all match.

reviews.question: What does a Malfunction disable and leave usable, where can it never be placed, and does it change an Engine token or harm an already-hibernating Character?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Malfunction makes Room Action and its Computer unavailable. 2. Searching still works; repair can remove marker. 3. Never placed in Nest, Room Covered With Slime, or unexplored Room. 4. Does not change Engine token/status; Hibernatorium Malfunction does not affect already-hibernated Character.
reviews.expected_answer: Disables Room Action and Computer; Search still works. Never in Nest or Room Covered In Slime. Special Rooms can malfunction; Engine Working/Damaged unaffected and already-hibernating Characters unaffected. Repair cards/Tools can remove marker.
reviews.reason: Correct disabled Room Action/Computer, usable Search/repair, excluded Rooms/unexplored locations and unchanged Engine/sleeper status.

reviews.question: Which Items may be hidden, what do other players see, what is the Inventory limit, and what must happen on use? How are Heavy Items/Objects, added Items and Duct Tape handled?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Normal Item cards hidden in card holder; others see backs/colors. 2. No Inventory size limit; show any Item when used. 3. Heavy Items/Objects are visible and occupy one of two Hand slots; max two carried. 4. Heavy Objects include Egg, Corpse, Carcass. Weapons searched start with 1 Ammo; never exceed printed capacity. Add Items attach to another card and count as one. Duct Tape combines two Heavy Items into one Hand slot, not Objects.
reviews.expected_answer: Normal Items hidden in unlimited Inventory, others see backs/colors; used Item shown. Heavy Items/Objects public in two Hands, third requires dropping one. Added Items act as one with base card. Duct Tape combines two Heavy Items into one Hand, never Objects.
reviews.reason: Hidden unlimited Inventory, public Hand items, use visibility, attachments and Duct Tape's Item-only exception match the key. Maximum two Hands plus the stated Duct Tape exception addresses the asked handling.

reviews.question: What happens to an Item versus an Object voluntarily dropped, when and at what Action cost may you drop, and how do found Weapons differ from starting Weapons in Ammo?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Dropped Objects stay in Room; dropped Items are lost/discarded. 2. Drop free at any time during your turn, no Action. 3. Searched Weapons come with 1 Ammo; starting Weapon loaded to its printed capacity.
reviews.expected_answer: Drop freely during own turn no Action; Objects stay in Room, Items discarded/lost. Found Weapon has 1 Ammo versus starting fully loaded, neither exceeds capacity.
reviews.reason: Correct free own-turn drop, Objects staying versus Items being discarded and searched-one versus starting-full Ammo.

reviews.question: How does Search choose its deck, draw and keep cards, return the rejected card, change the Item Counter, and handle zero Items, Special Rooms and Blue Items?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Search uses Room color: Red/Yellow/Green matching; white lets choose any. Draw 2 from one deck, keep 1. 2. Return rejected card face down to bottom of that deck. 3. Each Search lowers Item Counter by 1; at zero cannot use Search Action, except Scout Scavenging. 4. Special Rooms do not permit Searching; Blue Crafted Items cannot be searched for.
reviews.expected_answer: Search Action: choose one matching Red/Yellow/Green deck, white may choose any ONE, draw two, keep one, put rejected card at BOTTOM of same deck, not shuffle. Lower counter one, zero prevents Search except e.g. Scavenging; Special Rooms cannot Search. Blue Items only Craft.
reviews.reason: Correct single matching/white-choice deck, draw two/keep one, bottom return, counter reduction/zero exception and Special/Blue restrictions.

reviews.question: How does Craft pay its Action and components, must the result be available, can you inspect the deck, and what Crafted Items exist?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Craft Item Basic Action costs one Action card plus discard two Item cards with blue Component icons matching result's gray icons. 2. Result must be available in Craft deck. 3. May inspect Craft deck at any time. 4. Antidote flame+medical cross; Taser battery/lightning+tool; Flamethrower flame+tool; Molotov flame+fabric.
reviews.expected_answer: Cost one Action card plus discard two Items with blue component icons matching two grey result icons, choose/take available card not random draw; unavailable cannot build. May inspect deck any time. Antidote, Taser, Flamethrower, Molotov Cocktail.
reviews.reason: Correct Basic Action card payment, two matching blue-icon Items, availability/deck inspection and all four Crafted Items.

reviews.question: Who pays for a Trade and who may join; can you give something for nothing, exchange Ammo, or need a separate Pick Up Action for a searched Heavy Item?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Only initiator pays one Action card; any Characters in Room may agree to trade with each other. 2. May give Item/Object for nothing, but empty no-intent trade disallowed; honest negotiation can end without exchange. 3. Characters cannot exchange Ammo. 4. Heavy Items found by Searching need no separate Pick Up Action; pickup Basic Action is for Heavy Objects.
reviews.observed_evidence: Trade; FAQ Actions 1–2; Items and Objects
reviews.expected_answer: Initiator pays one Action card; Characters in same Room may agree to exchange Items/Objects including gifts. Cannot exchange Ammo. Pick Up Heavy Object cost one applies Corpses/Carcasses/Eggs, not searched Heavy Items.
reviews.reason: Initiator alone pays; any same-Room parties may exchange/gift, Ammo cannot be exchanged and searched Heavy Items need no pickup Action.

reviews.question: How do you reveal Weaknesses: what Object corresponds to each card, where must it be, is it consumed, who benefits and must you personally research for a Discover Weakness Objective?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Research corresponding Object: Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Egg. 2. Object must be present in Laboratory. 3. Object is retained, not consumed; Weakness revealed face up on Intruder board. 4. All players benefit. For Discover Weakness Objective, anyone may research it before game end; you need not do it personally.
reviews.expected_answer: Character Corpse, Intruder Egg, Intruder Carcass correspond to three face-down slots. Research matching Object present in Laboratory, carried or uncarried, reveal and leave card on board, Object not consumed. Discovered rules benefit all; anyone can do research for Objective.
reviews.reason: Names all three corresponding Object types, requires the Object in Laboratory, retains it, reveals the Weakness for everyone and permits any researcher for the Objective.

reviews.question: What are the common prerequisites and cost for Room Actions, what does a Computer icon itself do, and how does Fire affect Room Actions or Searching?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Usually in that Room, cost 2 Action cards; forbidden in Combat or Room with Malfunction. 2. Computer icon itself does nothing except indicate a Computer that a Malfunction disables / Computer-dependent abilities use. 3. Fire does not prevent Room Actions or Searching; character wound applies when ending own round in Fire.
reviews.expected_answer: Cost two Action cards, Character in matching Room unless explicit special ability, no Combat or Malfunction. Computer icon only significant when another rule references it, unavailable under Malfunction. Fire alone bars neither Room Action nor Search.
reviews.reason: Common Room requirements/cost, conditional meaning of Computer icon and Fire permitting both Room Actions and Search are explicit.

reviews.question: What exactly does the Armory recharge, by how much, and what limits apply?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Armory adds 2 Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons. 2. Not Classic Weapons and cannot exceed printed Ammo capacity.
reviews.expected_answer: Add two Ammo to one Energy Weapon, never Classic Weapons, never above printed capacity.
reviews.reason: Adds two Ammo to one Energy Weapon, excludes Classic Weapons and obeys capacity.

reviews.question: What are the three mutually exclusive Emergency Room treatments; does dressing remove the Wound or merely its effect, and do identical Serious Wound effects stack?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Choose one: Dress all Serious Wounds; Heal one Dressed Serious Wound; or Heal all Light Wounds. 2. Dressing flips card face down and ignores effect, does not remove wound/count. 3. Identical Serious Wound effects do not stack, though each counts toward three-wound limit.
reviews.expected_answer: Dress all Serious OR heal one dressed Serious OR heal all Light. Dress flips/ignores effect but retains Serious count; identical Serious effects do not stack.
reviews.reason: Gives all three alternative treatments, dressing's retained wound count and nonstacking duplicate effects.

reviews.question: What does sending a Signal actually do and what is its game use; can Comms be absent from a normal game?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Send Signal places a Status marker on your Character board's Signal space; used only for relevant Objective. 2. Comms Room is always aboard in standard setup.
reviews.expected_answer: Comms Room Action puts Status marker on own Signal space, used for Objectives only. Basic Room so always aboard.
reviews.reason: Signal marker location and Objective-only use are correct; Comms is always aboard.

reviews.question: How does Fire Control affect a chosen Room and its Intruders if the Room has Fire, or has none?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Fire Control chooses any one Room and discards its Fire marker if present. 2. All Intruders there run away in random directions by drawing an Event card per Intruder; works even if Room had no Fire.
reviews.expected_answer: Choose any one Room, remove Fire if present; all its Intruders flee random directions, one Event card drawn per Intruder. Works with no Fire.
reviews.reason: Any selected Room loses Fire if present and all Intruders flee with individual Event cards even without Fire.

reviews.question: Describe starting, stopping and restarting Self-Destruct, advancing it, the yellow threshold, its final space, a jump while active and a Character already hibernating.
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Generator starts by placing marker on first green space; stopping removes marker; new sequence restarts at green. 2. Advances one space with Time each turn; first yellow makes it unstoppable and unlocks Pods once; final skull explodes ship. Later yellow does not unlock again if relocked. 3. If jump occurs while active, ship is considered destroyed. 4. Character cannot initiate while anyone hibernates; Coolant Leak Event can. Hibernating Characters die on destruction.
reviews.expected_answer: Start marker first green; advance with Time. Stop removes it, restart green. First yellow irreversible/unlocks all Pods, which can relock; subsequent yellow spaces do NOT re-unlock them. Skull or jump with active sequence destroys ship. Characters cannot initiate sequence with anyone hibernating, but Coolant Leak Event can start it despite sleepers.
reviews.reason: Correct sequence start/stop/restart, synchronized advancement, first-yellow irreversibility/unlock, later-yellow exception, destruction and sleeper/Event distinction.

reviews.question: Which Room can Airlock Control target, what Door condition is required, what happens immediately, and what cancels or completes the procedure and when?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Target any one OTHER Yellow Room. 2. Its connected Corridors must contain no Destroyed Doors. 3. Automatically close every Door around it and place Procedure token there. 4. At current Player Phase end, if all Doors remain closed, everything in Room dies and Fire marker removed; opening any Door first cancels.
reviews.expected_answer: Any other Yellow Room with no Destroyed Doors in connected Corridors; close every connected Door, mark procedure. Opening any before Player Phase end removes token/cancels. All closed after all players pass kills all Characters/Intruders immediately, remove token and Fire.
reviews.reason: Other Yellow target, no Destroyed Doors, immediate closure/token, opening cancellation and end-of-Player-Phase lethal completion/removing Fire are explicit. Procedure-token cleanup is not an independently requested outcome here.

reviews.question: When does Cabins increase a hand and to what size; what disables it and is it a paid Room Action?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. At start of new turn, Character in Cabins with no Intruders draws one extra Action card (hand 6). 2. Malfunction disables it. 3. Passive, not a paid Room Action.
reviews.expected_answer: Passive at start of new turn draws to six instead of five if Character there and no Intruders; Malfunction disables. No paid Action.
reviews.reason: Correct passive start-of-turn hand six with no Intruders and Malfunction disabling; no paid Room Action.

reviews.question: Can Command Center select a distant Room and individually open some Doors and close others, including a Destroyed Door?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Command Center can choose any Room, including distant. 2. Open/Close any chosen Doors in its connected Corridors; choice need not be uniform. 3. Destroyed Door cannot be closed again except Plasma Torch, so not closable by this action.
reviews.expected_answer: Choose any one Room and individually open/close any connected Doors, need not all same. Destroyed Door cannot close except Plasma Torch.
reviews.reason: Allows any distant Room and individual Door choices while excluding closure of Destroyed Doors except Plasma Torch.

reviews.question: What can Engine Control Room check or change and how do Malfunctions in an Engine Room affect that check?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Engine Control Room checks status of all three Engines; cannot change them. 2. Works even if an Engine Room has Malfunction; Engine Room Malfunction affects Room Action only and never Engine status.
reviews.expected_answer: Check status of all three Engines even if corresponding Engine Room malfunctions; cannot change status from Control Room.
reviews.reason: Checks all three Engines without changing them and ignores an Engine Room's Malfunction for that check.

reviews.question: What does Hatch Control System change and how does Monitoring Room inspect a location: explored or unexplored, what components, secrecy and replacement?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Hatch Control flips one Pod token between Locked and Unlocked. 2. Monitoring secretly looks at any one unexplored Room tile and Exploration token. 3. You may lie about what saw; then replace both tile and token in same location.
reviews.observed_evidence: Room Actions: Hatch Control; Monitoring Room
reviews.expected_answer: Hatch flips one Pod Locked/Unlocked. Monitoring secretly looks at one unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, replaces both, may lie.
reviews.reason: Hatch flips one Pod; Monitoring checks only an unexplored tile plus token privately and replaces both, with lying allowed.

reviews.question: Does entering Room Covered With Slime require an Action to acquire Slime, can it have an Item Counter or Malfunction, can Slime stack, and does showering extinguish Fire?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Entering Room Covered With Slime automatically places Slime marker; no separate Action. 2. No Item count set; Malfunction cannot be placed. 3. Slime max one; further does nothing. 4. Shower removes Slime but does not extinguish Fire.
reviews.observed_evidence: Room Covered With Slime; Shower Room
reviews.expected_answer: Entry automatically gives Slime; no paid Action. No Item Counter, never Malfunction. Max one Slime, extra does nothing; Clothes/Shower remove. Shower does not remove Fire and Fire allowed there.
reviews.reason: Entry gives Slime automatically; no counter/Malfunction, no stacking and Shower does not extinguish Fire.

reviews.question: In Cockpit what can you learn or change, who sees the information, what does Destination refer to and which restrictions apply after someone hibernates or an Intruder is present?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Cockpit allows secretly check Coordinates or set Destination by moving marker. 2. Check is private; may lie and replace card. 3. Marker selects one of four destination entries on Coordinates card. 4. Cannot Set Destination with Intruder in Cockpit or change after anyone hibernates.
reviews.expected_answer: Check Coordinates secretly and replace, may lie and should remember; Set Destination moves marker to chosen track space referring to one of four card destinations. No Set with Intruder in Cockpit; no change after any hibernation; common Room prerequisites apply.
reviews.reason: Private Coordinates check/replacement, Destination marker's selected entry and restrictions from Intruder presence or hibernation are explicit.

reviews.question: How does Engine checking differ from repairing/breaking; what can stay secret, what must be announced and do you need a prior check or functioning Engine Room?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Check Engine secretly views top token. Repair/Break examines both and restacks in any order using Repairs Action or Tools Item. 2. You need not say whether repaired. 3. Must announce if order changed. 4. No prior check or functioning Engine Room required; works despite Malfunction.
reviews.expected_answer: Check secretly top token only may lie. Repairs Action or Tools permits take both tokens secretly restack any order. Need announce whether order changed, not whether repaired. Works without prior check and despite Malfunction. Top true status, two Working needed.
reviews.reason: Separates top-token check from two-token restacking, names repair mechanisms, keeps repair result secret, announces changed order and waives prior check/functioning Room.

reviews.question: When is hibernation legal, what roll and failure condition apply, what leaves play on success, and which later ship actions are forbidden? Does later Malfunction wake sleepers?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. May hibernate only Time blue, present in Hibernatorium, no Intruder or Malfunction there; cost 2 Action cards. 2. Roll Noise; if Intruder appears/reaches room attempt fails. 3. Success removes miniature and player stops participating until end checks. 4. After anyone hibernates no Character can change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct; Coolant Leak Event exception. Later Malfunction does not wake/harm sleeper.
reviews.expected_answer: Only Time on blue, functioning Hibernatorium without Intruder; Room Action cost two, Noise roll, appearing Intruder fails. Success remove Character miniature and participation until end checks. Destination change and starting Self-Destruct prohibited. Later Malfunction has no effect on sleepers.
reviews.reason: Blue-Time presence/cost/no-Intruder/no-Malfunction prerequisites, Noise failure, miniature removal, later prohibited Character actions and sleeper immunity to later Malfunction match.

reviews.question: What ends the game when Time runs out or the last active Character leaves/dies/hibernates; how is an active Self-Destruct resolved and do Intruders die from a normal jump?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Time final red: immediate hyperspace jump; every nonhibernating Character aboard dies. 2. Last alive, nonhibernating Character dies/hibernates/launches: end game. 3. If Self-Destruct active, advance to final red; otherwise Time to final red, resolve effect. 4. Intruders unharmed by normal jump; they die if ship explodes.
reviews.expected_answer: Time final red immediate jump, awake aboard die; Intruders unharmed. Last alive non-hibernating aboard leaves/dies/hibernates: advance active Self-Destruct to final red and destroy ship, else advance Time final red and jump. Then survival/victory checks if survivors.
reviews.reason: Final-red jump kills awake Characters but not Intruders; last-active end advances the active sequence or Time and resolves destruction/jump correctly.

reviews.question: Can a Character directly attack another, and may an Action still harm other crew indirectly? Give source-supported examples.
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Characters cannot directly attack another Character. 2. Indirect harm is possible: lock someone in burning Room, activate Self-Destruct with crew aboard, or throw Grenade into Room with other crew.
reviews.expected_answer: Never directly attack Characters; indirect harm permitted, e.g. grenade at Intruder with crew present, trap in burning Room, Self-Destruct.
reviews.reason: Explicitly prohibits direct attacks and supplies the source-supported indirect-harm examples from the frozen summary.

reviews.question: You must place an Adult but all eight models are on board. What explicit procedure applies, and what if an Intruder enters an unexplored Room by movement?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. If all 8 Adult models on board, remove all Adults not in Combat, return their tokens to bag if possible, then place Adult in Encounter Room. If all 8 in Combat summary expressly says procedure unresolved. 2. Intruder entering unexplored Room by movement remains there; do not reveal tile or Exploration token.
reviews.observed_evidence: Adult overflow; Intruders in unexplored Rooms
reviews.expected_answer: Remove ALL Adults not in Combat and return corresponding tokens to bag if possible, then place Adult in Encounter Room. Moving Intruder into unexplored Room does not reveal Room/token and is not removed. If all eight are in Combat, the source supplies no executable resolution for freeing a model; do not invent one.
reviews.reason: Gives the complete available-model procedure and explicitly leaves all-eight-in-Combat model supply unresolved; movement into unexplored Rooms leaves Intruder and tile/token unrevealed. This matches the factual key, but the actual asked model-supply branch remains unresolved, requiring strict Partial.

reviews.question: For shooting, describe the target-size restrictions of the small curled and larger curved Intruder die symbols; what happens on those same symbols in Melee against an ineligible target?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Small curled symbol hits Larva/Creeper only; other Shoot targets are missed. 2. Larger curved hits Larva/Creeper/Adult; misses Breeder/Queen. 3. In Melee same target eligibility applies; ineligible target is a miss and Character suffers 1 Serious Wound.
reviews.expected_answer: Small curled symbol hits Larva/Creeper for one only; larger curved hits Larva/Creeper/Adult for one only; other targets missed. Same target restrictions in Melee; miss causes Serious Wound.

source_references.basis: Visual inspection of matching original-edition diagram/icons

reviews.reason: Both requested symbol-size eligibility sets and Melee ineligible-target miss/Serious Wound are explicit. One Injury on eligible hits is unasked context in a question about target-size restrictions.

reviews.question: At the final Contamination check, a survivor has no Larva and every Contamination card scans non-Infected. Must they perform the four-card draw or remove those cards, and does an earlier launched Pod escape the Objective check?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. With no Larva, scan every Contamination card in deck/hand/discard. 2. If none Infected, do not shuffle/draw four; do not remove non-Infected cards. 3. Earlier launched Pod still undergoes final Contamination check and Objective check.
reviews.expected_answer: No four-card draw unless infected found or Larva on board; end scan does not instruct removing non-infected. Pod passenger still needs surviving Contamination check and chosen Objective fulfillment.
reviews.reason: No infected/no Larva means no four-card test or card removal; Pod passengers still undergo Contamination and Objective checks.

reviews.question: Which two component symbols are required for each Crafted Item: Antidote, Taser, Flamethrower and Molotov Cocktail? Describe the symbols rather than guessing Item-card names.
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Flame + medical cross. 2. Battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool. 3. Flame + screwdriver/tool. 4. Flame + folded cloth/fabric.
reviews.expected_answer: Antidote: flame and medical cross. Taser: battery/lightning and screwdriver/tool. Flamethrower: flame and screwdriver/tool. Molotov Cocktail: flame and folded cloth/fabric. Each takes two matching blue-component Item cards.

source_references.basis: Visual inspection of matching original-edition diagram/icons

reviews.reason: All four component pairs are supplied in the same ordered sequence as the named Items in the question, using symbols rather than invented Item-card names.

reviews.question: What defines being in Combat, how do In Combat Only and Out of Combat Only restrictions work, and may an unmarked Action or Item be used in either situation? Do Eggs cause Combat?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. In Combat whenever Intruder in your Room. 2. Apply explicit In Combat Only/Out of Combat Only restrictions. Basic Actions in Combat limited to Shoot, Melee, Basic Movement as Escape; Room Actions forbidden. 3. Unmarked card/Item Actions usable in or out subject to requirements. 4. Eggs are not Intruders and do not cause Combat.
reviews.expected_answer: Sharing Room with Intruder defines Combat, not Eggs. In Combat Only requires it, Out of Combat Only requires none. Unmarked card/Item actions can be used in either subject to requirements; Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape. No Room Actions or Quest activation in Combat.
reviews.reason: Sharing a Room with an Intruder defines Combat; explicit restrictions govern, unmarked card/Item Actions are usable in either state and Eggs do not cause Combat.

reviews.question: For an Objective that Player X cannot survive, must you personally kill them, does hibernating or escaping count as death, and how does only survivor differ? What must your own Character do regardless?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Must be dead by end; do not have to kill personally. 2. Hibernating or escaped Character counts as surviving, so does not satisfy cannot survive. 3. Only survivor means no other Character survives. 4. Regardless, your own Character must survive and fulfill Objective.
reviews.expected_answer: X must be dead at game end; need not be killed by own Actions; hibernating or escaping alive is not death. Only survivor means nobody else survives. Own Character must survive by launched Pod or successful hibernation, plus meet Objective.
reviews.reason: Target must be dead without personal killing; hibernation/escape is survival, only survivor excludes all other survivors, and own survival/Objective remain required.

reviews.question: If a Door token must be placed and none are in the pool, what happens? How are Open, Closed and Destroyed Doors represented, and may two Door tokens share one Corridor or be placed in Technical Corridors?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. If pool empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on board. 2. Open is no token; Closed is standing token; Destroyed lying token. 3. Max one per Corridor. 4. Doors never placed in Technical Corridors.
reviews.expected_answer: Take any Door token elsewhere on board and move to required Corridor. Open no token, Closed standing, Destroyed lying. Max one per Corridor; none in Technical Corridors.
reviews.reason: Moves an existing Door if supply empty, gives all representations, one-per-Corridor and Technical-Corridor ban.

reviews.question: The first Character dies while the ship's Pods are Locked. What happens to every Pod immediately, and can they subsequently be Locked again?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. On first Character death all Escape Pods automatically unlock immediately. 2. This applies to every Pod. 3. They may later be locked/unlocked normally through Hatch Control etc.; summary notes ambiguity about whether later deaths re-unlock after relocking, but this question asks subsequent locking: yes, Pods may subsequently be Locked again.
reviews.expected_answer: All Escape Pods immediately become Unlocked. They may subsequently be Locked and Unlocked normally, for example through Hatch Control System.
reviews.reason: Explicit first-death unlock of every Pod and subsequent normal relocking are correct. Extra later-death ambiguity is truthful context outside this question.

reviews.question: What does the Storage Room's Search for an Item Room Action let you draw and keep, where exactly does the rejected card go, and what are the common Room Action cost and restrictions?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Room Action draws 2 cards from chosen Red/Yellow/Green deck and keeps one. 2. Other returned face down to bottom of that deck. 3. Room Actions cost 2 Action cards, require in Room, forbidden in Combat or Malfunction. Storage can be used repeatedly even at Item Counter zero; counter limits Search Action card only.
reviews.expected_answer: Pay two Action cards while in the functioning Storage Room and out of Combat. Choose the Red, Yellow or Green Item deck, draw two cards, keep one, and put the other at the bottom of that deck.
reviews.reason: Correct deck choice/draw/keep/bottom return and common Room Action cost, presence, Combat and Malfunction restrictions.

reviews.question: While in the Nest, how do you take an Egg still represented on the Intruder board, what does that Action cost, and what happens immediately afterward? How does this differ from picking up a previously dropped Egg token in your Room?

requested_parts.part: Ordinary dropped-Egg pickup does not instruct a Noise roll
requested_parts.reason: The one-card Basic Action is named, but its absence of a Noise-roll instruction is not expressly answered.

reviews.observed_answer: 1. While in Nest, Room Action removes one Egg token from Intruder board and costs 2 Action cards. 2. Then roll Noise. 3. A dropped Egg is a Heavy Object in Room picked up with Pick Up Heavy Object Basic Action (1 card); it is no longer represented on Intruder board and returning it to Nest does not restore Nest total.
reviews.observed_evidence: Nest; Pick Up Heavy Object; Egg FAQ
reviews.expected_answer: Use the Nest's Take one Egg Room Action, costing two Action cards and subject to common Room Action restrictions. Take one Egg token from the Intruder board, then perform a Noise roll. The Egg is a Heavy Object and occupies a Hand slot. Picking up an already dropped Egg is the ordinary one-card Pick Up Heavy Object Basic Action; that pickup procedure does not itself instruct a Noise roll.
reviews.reason: Two-card Nest retrieval and subsequent Noise, versus one-card dropped-Object pickup, are correct. The contrast does not explicitly say that ordinary dropped-Egg pickup has no instructed Noise roll; no answer elsewhere can supply that missing distinction.

reviews.question: You perform the Action printed on a One Use Only Item. Besides paying its Action-card cost and showing it, what happens to the Item card after use?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Pay required Action-card cost and show Item card when used. 2. One Use Only Item card is discarded after use to appropriate Item discard pile.
reviews.observed_evidence: Actions from Item cards; Discard piles
reviews.expected_answer: Discard the Item card to the appropriate Item discard pile after using it. This is in addition to discarding the Action cards needed to pay its Action cost.
reviews.reason: Explicitly discards the One Use Only Item to its appropriate discard after use, in addition to Action-card cost/showing.

reviews.question: For a rule concerned with the Character's arrival on Earth, where is a Character in a launched Escape Pod treated as having arrived? Does this establish that the ship itself reached Earth?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Launched Pod occupants count as arriving on Earth. 2. This does not establish that ship reached Earth; ship destination is separately determined by Coordinates and Destination marker.
reviews.expected_answer: Any Character in a launched Escape Pod is always treated as having arrived on Earth. This is the Character's status and does not establish that the ship reached Earth; the ship's destination and survival are checked separately. The passenger still undergoes the normal endgame Contamination and Objective checks.
reviews.reason: Launched Pod counts as arriving on Earth without proving the ship's destination; separate Coordinates/marker determination is explicit. Final survivor checks are outside the asked implication.

reviews.question: While waiting in an Escape Pod, must you roll Noise when Adult bag development calls for it?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Yes. Waiting Pod occupant remains treated as present in Section for Noise rolls from bag development.
reviews.expected_answer: Yes. Waiting Character is treated as present in the corresponding Room and rolls Noise.
reviews.reason: Explicitly requires the waiting occupant's bag-development Noise roll as present in the Section.

reviews.question: A Malfunction is placed in the Evacuation Section while you are already waiting in its Pod. Can you launch, wait or exit, and what does that Malfunction prevent?

reviews.question: When Adult bag development triggers Noise, when does the drawn Adult token return, and may a triggered Encounter draw that very token?

reviews.question: Where do discarded/dead Intruder tokens go, and can they be reused later?

reviews.question: Self-Destruct reaches its first yellow space, Pods unlock, then are relocked. Does reaching the next yellow space unlock them again?

reviews.question: Does destroying the ship fulfill Objectives to kill the Queen or destroy the Nest; does that alone make your Character a winner?

reviews.question: May you intentionally spend an empty Trade Action with no intention of exchange; what if honest negotiations end without a trade?

reviews.question: What kind of Action activates a Quest Item, may it be done in Combat, and does a Room Malfunction prevent it?

reviews.question: Which Basic Actions can be used in Combat; can you Trade, Craft or Pick Up an Object there? What about permitted card or Item Actions?

reviews.reason: Lists the exhaustive permitted Basic Actions, excludes Trade/Craft/pickup and permits appropriate card/Item Actions under their restrictions.

reviews.question: Can Soldier use Covering Fire only on themselves, and how are direction, Noise and Surprise targeting handled when moving two Characters?
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone. 2. Both Characters choose direction; then one Noise roll. If Encounter, compare Surprise against Soldier.

reviews.question: How does Full Auto calculate damage and consume Ammo?

reviews.question: When can Nerves of Steel be chosen relative to seeing the Attack card, and may it protect you when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack?

reviews.question: Careful Movement or Reconnaissance reveals a Danger/Silence Exploration token. Does that automatic result apply or the movement ability?

reviews.question: May Captain use Order while personally in Combat; may Intercom force someone else to Move out of Combat and what rules apply?

reviews.question: Can you Interrupt a Captain Order played remotely via Intercom when you are not in the Captain Room; does passing bar playing Interruption?

reviews.question: After two Actions your hand is empty. Do you automatically pass then, and what timing consequence can Fire or Bleeding have?

reviews.question: Rest scans several Infected cards while no Larva was on your board. Can the scan kill you from multiple infected cards; when can Rest be fatal?

reviews.question: Scientist uses Intranet to research an Object while carrying it outside the Laboratory. Can that reveal a Weakness?

reviews.question: Describe Antidote: scan scope, removed cards, new Contamination, reshuffling, hand retention and passing; how does Surgery differ?

reviews.question: On exploration, where are Slime, Fire, Malfunction and Door effects placed, and which Corridor receives the Door?
